# PM lessons: Briefs & scripts

Mistakes the PM made once and the rule that came out of each.

nodes.l: A deal paid upfront still sends its revised script
nodes.b:
When: A brand that paid 100% before the video sends script notes, and the card comes back to 5- Script Approval with the updated script
Do: Send the revised script to the brand in its thread as for any live deal, with only the newest version in the PDF; a Paid stage means the money is in, not that the work is done
Never: Never treat a Paid deal with a Script Sent Date as finished while its video is not posted, and never send the old and the updated script together in one PDF
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Brand script feedback moves the card to 4.8- Script Changes; back at 5 the revised script
nodes.b:
When: A brand sends changes on a script we already sent
Do: Move every card of that deal still in scripting to 4.8- Script Changes, put the brand's notes on the card, and tag Rudraksh. When the card is moved back to 5, send the script again as the revised version, all cards ready together in one email
Never: Never leave the card at 5 or 4.5 after brand feedback (nobody can tell it needs work), and never treat a card returning to 5 after changes as already sent
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A card moved to 5 sends its script, including later videos of a posted deal and revised sc
nodes.b:
When: A video card reaches 5- Script Approval (from 4.5 Internal Review or any earlier status)
Do: Send the script unless that exact version already went. Every Script email records a fingerprint of each script it carried, and a card at 5 whose script differs from the sent version goes again as a revised script
Never: Never let the deal's stage (Posted after video 1 went live) block the scripts of its other videos, and never re-send a script whose content hasn't changed
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A deal paid upfront still sends its script when the card reaches Script Approval
nodes.b:
When: A deal is already Paid or Invoiced (upfront payment) and its video card moves to 5- Script Approval
Do: Send the script email the same way as any other deal, the same day
Never: Never skip or delay the script because the deal stage is already Paid or Invoiced
Seen 2 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A brief is not a contract, even when the email mentions the agreement
nodes.b:
When: A brand email carries a PDF and talks about a contract or agreement
Do: Treat it as a contract only when the file is named or written as one, or the brand says it is the contract to sign. If the email calls the file a brief or says the agreement comes later ("once you confirm, I will share the formal agreement"), it is a brief: file it on the deal's card and answer what the brand asked (usually a date for Harsh).
Never: Send "thanks for sending the contract, we'll review and sign it" or a Contract alert for a brief.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: The brand's brief file always lands on the card and reaches the script writer
nodes.b:
When: A brand sends the brief as a PDF, Word or slides file, in any email of the thread
Do: Attach the file on the video card inside the brief and tell the script writer it's there; if the email with the file was held or too big, fetch it from Gmail
Never: Never write a 'Source email' section (sender, subject, date) on a card, and never leave the brief file only in Gmail
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: No money for the team, but the brief's own content words still reach the script writer
nodes.b:
When: A brand note uses a money word about the video itself (budget pressure, Black Friday price on the end card, it cost me a coffee, paid partnership label)
Do: Send that line to the script writer. Anything the money filter does hold back goes to Harsh in #pm so nothing disappears silently
Never: Drop a content note because it contains the word budget, price or cost
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A deal past the brief always has a video card
nodes.b:
When: A deal reaches Brief Received or later, including deals opened by the system check or by hand
Do: Make the card with the brief, link it in the deal's Linked Video and tell the script writer once
Never: Leave a deal with a brief and no card, so nobody is writing the script
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Script notes go to the card still being scripted, never to a filmed video
nodes.b:
When: A deal has several videos and the brand sends script notes or a script approval
Do: Put the notes on the sibling cards at status 5 or lower (CapCut x Chris (2), (3)) and ping the script writer with those cards
Never: Move a card that is filmed, with the brand or approved back to 4 or 6, or put the next script's notes on it
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A brand describing its review process is not an approval
nodes.b:
When: A brand email mentions script review, approval or filming as steps still to come, before any script was sent
Do: Count a script as approved only when the brand approves a script we actually sent (Script Sent Date or a sent Script email). 'Upon our approval', 'send us the script for review' and a step-by-step guide are instructions: answer what they ask for now.
Never: Set Script Approved, move a card to 6 or draft a tool-access email when no script has been sent.
Seen 3 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Include the script link in the draft email
nodes.b:
When: Sending a script to the brand for review
Do: Add the Google Drive or Frame.io link to the script in the email body so the brand can access it immediately.
Never: Send a script email without the link to the actual file
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Draft edit.

nodes.l: A script the creator's team sends by hand is a sent script
nodes.b:
When: Our side (the creator or their team) emails the script into the brand's thread before the PM's own Script email goes out
Do: Record it like the PM's own send: Script Sent Date and Last Our Reply from that email, Next Action 'waiting on the brand to approve', and retire the PM's waiting Script draft.
Never: Leave the deal saying 'send the script' or with an empty Script Sent Date, because follow-ups and the 'script at 5 with no email' check then work from wrong facts.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: No team ping for work that hasn't started
nodes.b:
When: A brand asks to pause, or any update arrives, on a deal with no brief and no video card yet
Do: Keep the hold on the deal and keep following up with the brand, but only tell the script writer or an editor when a video card exists for that deal, meaning work was actually handed to them.
Never: Never ping Rudraksh or an editor to stop or change work on a video they were never given.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Scripts at Script Approval go to the brand
nodes.b:
When: A card reaches 5- Script Approval
Do: Share the script with the brand in the deal's existing thread (WhatsApp deals: tell Harsh). When a sponsor card reaches 5 and no deal links to it, find the brand's open deal and link the card to it instead of only alerting "script ready, no deal".
Never: Leave it unsent or send it in a new thread.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

nodes.l: An approval with the brand's own script is an approval
nodes.b:
When: Brand/platform says 'Approved Idea, Script', 'validated version', or Next Step 'Draft video'
Do: Card to To Film, deal Script Approved, save their version as the final script.
Never: Send it to Rudraksh as changes or a brief update.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

When: Writing cards, briefs, team pings, the access page
Do: Keep only creative content.
Never: Mention a rate, price, fee, budget, $ or payment.
Seen 3 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

When: A deal covers 2+ reels, or a brief arrives for the next reel
Do: Make a card per reel; put the next reel's brief on its own card.
Never: Put reel 2's brief on reel 1's finished card.
Seen 4 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

# PM lessons: Deals & data

Mistakes the PM made once and the rule that came out of each.

nodes.l: Unsure how to reply still means the new deal gets opened
nodes.b:
When: The two readers disagree on a creator loop-in or an agreed brand deal that has no deal row for its thread
Do: Open the deal flagged Needs you, tell the team in #pm-alerts, and write nothing to the brand so Harsh replies himself
Never: Never drop the email with nothing in Notion just because the PM doesn't know what to reply
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A contract the brand sends is always filed, even if the email only says  Please check that
nodes.b:
When: A brand email in a deal thread carries an agreement or contract PDF, whatever the email text says, even when the email has no text at all
Do: Save it to CONTRACTS and the deal, send it to WhatsApp, send the fixed contract_ack, and move the deal's next step to the creator reviewing and signing
Never: Never skip a brand's contract as if it were our own signed copy. Only our side or the creator sends contracts back signed
Seen 2 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Every deal is checked within a couple of heartbeats
nodes.b:
When: The heartbeat's deal emails step runs out of time before the end of the deal list
Do: Start the next run at the deal the last run stopped before, and show 'N of M deals, next: ...' in the step
Never: Leave the deals past one run's reach to wait hours for a rotating start to drift onto them
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Live links sent with the invoice count as the links email
nodes.b:
When: A deal's live links went to the brand inside another email (usually the invoice email) and a Posted links step comes up
Do: Treat the links as sent: fill Links Sent Date from that email and draft nothing more about the links. If a reminder is due, it is a payment chase, written as one.
Never: Draft a Posted links email for links the brand already has, or put another email's body (a payment chase) under the Posted links kind.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A sign link on the brand's own domain is a contract, and every contract gets acknowledged
nodes.b:
When: A brand sends a contract to sign, as a file, an e-sign service link or a link on their own site (agreements.<agency>.com/sign/...)
Do: Save it in CONTRACTS as Needs signing, send it to Harsh and Pratham on WhatsApp, and send the brand the fixed contract_ack reply at once
Never: Treat it as a plain brand reply because the link is not DocuSign or PandaDoc, or leave the brand with no answer
Seen 2 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A brief after an agreed price always opens a deal, wherever it lands
nodes.b:
When: A brand that agreed a rate sends the brief (or a creator forwards a brand email) in the creator's own inbox
Do: Open the deal at Brief Received with the agreed rate, the brief link and the brand's Message-ID, create the video card, and when the brand chases, ask Harsh for the date. A creator forwarding a brand email to noocapcollab is our side handing it over, never 'our reply to the brand'.
Never: Leave the lead at 'Waiting on brand' after the brief came, or count the creator's forward as having answered the brand.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: An agency contact pitching another product is a new lead, not a reply on their old deal
nodes.b:
When: A brand or agency contact who already has a live deal writes on a new thread about a different product or campaign (new subject naming another brand, "partnership opportunity", a rate question)
Do: Treat it as a new inquiry: file it on its own lead or deal for that product, take the rate or terms question to Harsh, and leave the old deal's stage, Next Action and memory as they were
Never: Match it to the old deal only because the sender's address is the same, or set the old deal to Waiting on us with the other product's terms
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A script we offer once the brand sends the brief is not a script we owe
nodes.b:
When: Our side (creator's team or NOOCAP) asks the brand for the contract or brief and says we will start the script once it arrives
Do: Record the brand as owing the brief and contract; Next Action is waiting on the brand, and follow-ups chase the brief on the normal 3-day rhythm.
Never: Turn it into 'Send <brand> the Script (promised today)', write 'We owe: contract and brief' in Deal Memory, or tell Harsh a script is due.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Inbox reader lists can arrive as one string
nodes.b:
When: Filing an email from the reader's answer
Do: Treat summary, we_promised and delivers as lists whatever shape the reader returns
Never: Let one oddly shaped field stop an email from being filed
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A brand saying 'got it, we'll review' leaves the next move with the brand
nodes.b:
When: A brand writes again only to confirm they received or can open what we sent and will come back with feedback
Do: Record it as the brand's latest email and set the deal to waiting on the brand, with the next check-in counted from that email
Never: Set the deal to 'Waiting on us', put it on Harsh's list or draft a reply to a plain acknowledgement
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Only our own inboxes speak for NOOCAP
nodes.b:
When: Reading an email in a deal thread that is signed by someone at an outside company (an agency or the brand's team)
Do: Treat anyone writing from a company domain that is not noocapcollab or a creator's own domain as the brand's side: record it as a brand reply, move Last Brand Reply, and let their address become the brand contact.
Never: File an agency's 'script is under review' or 'waiting for the client's approval' as our own email because the signer's first name matches one of our creators or the tone sounds like ours.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A brand email in the creator's inbox belongs to the deal of that brand contact
nodes.b:
When: A brand on a live deal writes only to the creator's own inbox (no reply-all), so the email has another Gmail thread id than the deal
Do: Match the deal by the sender's address (the deal's Brand Email) and creator, record the email on that deal, set Last Brand Reply and hand it to Harsh as Waiting on us; link a locked lead to the deal of that contact before any brand-name match. When that email approves the script, act on it as an approval: deal to Script Approved with the date, card to 6- To Film, and the tool-access email in the deal's own thread.
Never: Leave the deal on 'waiting for the brand' because only the lead was updated, or link a lead to another deal because the brand names overlap (Tripo 3D vs Hyper3D / Tripo 3D)
Seen 3 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A new deal in an old thread starts with nothing from the old deal's billing
nodes.b:
When: Opening a deal for a brand's next campaign or a new brief that arrived in an existing thread
Do: Start it at Inbound (or the stage the new emails really show) with empty invoice fields, its own Deal Memory about the new campaign only, and the brand's newest Message-ID. Billing, invoices and payment chases stay on the old deal.
Never: Copy the old deal's stage, Invoice Sent Date, Invoice Amount, invoice number or 'waiting for payment' memory onto the new deal; a copied Invoice Sent Date starts payment chases for money nobody owes.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: An invite to the brand's next campaign is a new deal
nodes.b:
When: A brand whose deal is posted, invoiced or paid invites the creator to a new campaign in the same thread, even inside an email about payment and without asking for a rate
Do: Open a deal of its own at Inbound (same thread, Needs Check), ask Harsh on WhatsApp whether the creator joins, and keep the payment news on the old deal
Never: Fold the invite into the finished deal's memory or Next Action, or treat it as a brief on the old deal
Seen 3 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A rate ask on a finished deal is a new inquiry
nodes.b:
When: A brand whose deal is already Posted, Invoiced or Paid writes in the same thread asking for our rate for something new (another video, an event, a session).
Do: Open a separate deal at Inbound for the new ask with the thread's IDs, and put the rate question to Harsh. Leave the finished deal's memory and stage as they were.
Never: Never fold the new ask into the finished deal or rewrite its Deal Memory, and never guess a rate.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A deal opened from our own handover email still needs the brand's address
nodes.b:
When: The creator's team writes 'please add noocapcollab to this thread' and the PM opens a deal from that email
Do: Set Brand Email to the brand person our email was written to (first To/Cc address that is not ours, the creator's or a no-reply robot), and copy the Thread CC
Never: Leave Brand Email empty because the email came from our side, so no reply or script can be addressed later
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A brand question is not a hold
nodes.b:
When: A brand asks us a question or says they could not do something on their side
Do: Treat it as a question we owe an answer to (ask Harsh once if only he knows) and keep the deal moving.
Never: Label it 'brand asked us to hold the work' or send a hold alert when the brand never said to pause.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Read the whole thread before acting
nodes.b:
When: Any brand email, especially agency threads
Do: Read the full conversation: a new brand in an agency thread is a new deal, earlier proof of payment counts, amounts come from what was agreed.
Never: Judge an email on its own.
Seen 4 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

When: Matching or totalling these deals
Do: Bluehost = Bluehost 2 (one deal); Chris's TRIPO and Inworld came from WhatsApp; Duncan's company and payment details go on his invoices.
Never: Count VIRASH, VEED or UTOPAI.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

# PM lessons: Emails

Mistakes the PM made once and the rule that came out of each.

nodes.l: Wrong details we sent are corrected before the brand's document is signed
nodes.b:
When: We sent a brand wrong facts (a creator's name, address, rate or date) and the brand answers with a document built on them, such as an agreement or invoice form
Do: Keep the correction alive after the brand's next email: answer that email with the right facts, ask them to fix the document, and tell Harsh on WhatsApp in the contract message that the document carries the wrong details so he does not sign it
Never: Retire the correction because the brand wrote again, or file the brand's document as ready to sign without saying it repeats our mistake
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Never invent a creator's legal or business details
nodes.b:
When: A brand asks for the creator's business name, legal name, legal address, contact email, tax ID or bank details (for an agreement, invoice or vendor form), in any email the PM writes
Do: Leave those details out of the email and ask Harsh on WhatsApp for them; answer the rest of the email (the script, the cut). Only details Harsh gave, or ones already on file word for word, ever go to a brand.
Never: Fill in a name, company, address or email that is not on file (no 'Lindsay Creative LLC', '123 Maple Street', 'name@noocap.com'), and never put agreement details inside a script, follow-up, tool-access or cut email.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: An e-sign notice gets no reply email
nodes.b:
When: An automated signing service (agreements@, PandaDoc, DocuSign, a 'Please sign' or 'Completed' notice with a sign link) emails a contract for a creator
Do: Send the contract and sign link to Harsh on WhatsApp once and link it to the right deal; a 'Completed' notice only records that it is signed.
Never: Never draft a reply to the signing service's address, never greet the campaign contact in it, and never promise to review or sign it 'shortly'.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A loop-in reply asks only for what the brand hasn't sent
nodes.b:
When: A creator's team loops noocapcollab into a brand thread
Do: Check the thread for a brief link or file and an attached contract, and ask only for what is missing
Never: Never ask the brand for a brief or contract that is already in the thread
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A rejected draft waits for a new email before it is written again
nodes.b:
When: Any draft that Harsh or the system check rejected, or that expired
Do: Draft it again only once the brand or we send a new email in that deal (the 3-day cooldown still caps the wait)
Never: Never write the same kind of email for the same deal again just because a day has passed and nothing in the thread changed
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Ask Harsh before drafting an answer to a brand question
nodes.b:
When: A brand email asks us something, inside a brief, script approval or video feedback
Do: Ask Harsh on WhatsApp with the brand's words and draft the email from his answer
Never: Never write an AI reply to the question before Harsh has answered it, because those drafts were rejected almost every time and cost two AI calls each
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A script, invoice or file email is never held for a missing attachment
nodes.b:
When: The second check reads a Script, Invoice or File email before it reaches Approvals
Do: Remember the file goes on at send time (Script PDF from the card, Invoice from Stripe, Send File); judge the email with that file attached.
Never: Hold a Script, Invoice or File email because the draft itself has no attachment yet.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A cut email also repeats any answer we already gave to the brand's open question
nodes.b:
When: A cut goes to the brand while the brand's latest message asks something our own earlier emails already answered (an account email, a code, a link)
Do: Hand over the cut and repeat that answer in one short sentence, word for word as we gave it. Read our own sent emails in the thread before saying anything is missing
Never: Never tell the writer to answer nothing else while the second check demands the question be answered: the two rules together held every cut for a brand with an open question
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Don't send 'ignore this' emails unless the error is critical
nodes.b:
When: An email was sent to the wrong thread or contained a minor mistake.
Do: If an email was sent by mistake, only send a correction if the brand is likely to be confused or act on the error. If it is minor or they have not noticed, stay silent to avoid calling attention to a mistake that might have gone unnoticed.
Never: Send an 'ignore the last email' correction for minor errors or if the brand is likely to have ignored or missed it.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Draft rejected.

nodes.l: A quoted line or a broken-up link is never the brand's question
nodes.b:
When: Reading what a brand asks in its newest email
Do: Cut the quoted history at a wrapped 'On ... wrote:' line and at the first '>' line, and ignore leftover pieces of links, before taking a question from the email
Never: Show Harsh our own quoted question, or a link fragment like 'd/12PP.../edit?', as the brand's question
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Trial and tool accounts brands ask for go to noocaptools@gmail.com
nodes.b:
When: A brand asks which email to use for a trial account, Pro access, credits or a tool login for the creator
Do: Give noocaptools@gmail.com
Never: Never give the creator's personal or business email (like duncan@buildroom.ai) for a trial account
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: One send per draft  an email that is already being sent can't be sent again
nodes.b:
When: Any send of a PM OUTBOX draft (Send in Approvals, WhatsApp send, sendoutbox hook, auto-send)
Do: Each send writes its own claim into Error, waits 2 seconds and reads it back; only the send whose claim is still there goes ahead, and a fresh claim (under 3 minutes) blocks any other send
Never: Never send a draft that another send has already claimed, and Claude never calls sendoutbox on a draft sitting in Approvals without first checking Harsh hasn't already pressed Send
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Publish-date confirmations send on their own
nodes.b:
When: The brand has approved the content and asks us to confirm we're ready to publish or when it goes live
Do: Send the fixed reply publish_date_confirm with the video card's POST DATE, no approval needed
Never: Never hold this for Harsh, never write a date that isn't the card's POST DATE, never send it when the card has no date
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A brand email nobody answered stays unread
nodes.b:
When: A brand email asks something of us (a question, a date, a confirmation, a reply) and the PM sends no reply and drafts none
Do: Leave it unread in noocapcollab Gmail so Harsh sees who is waiting, and only mark read once a reply went out or is in Approvals
Never: Never mark a waiting brand email read just because it was filed, logged or already seen by another run
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A brand chasing a promised posting gets a time from Harsh, never 'today' or 'finishing tou
nodes.b:
When: A brand asks when the approved video goes live, or chases a posting we said would happen today
Do: Give the posting time Harsh supplied, otherwise ask Harsh on WhatsApp for it before replying
Never: Write 'we will post it today/tomorrow/soon/now', 'Chris will post it today', 'we are going ahead and posting it now', 'we are posting it today', 'we're getting it posted right now', 'we are putting the finishing touches' or 'we're finalizing the video' without a time Harsh gave
Seen 3 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A fixed reply in Harsh's own words sends on its own, timing line included
nodes.b:
When: Saving a Reply Templates reply (Why has [template:...]) such as billing_on_approval
Do: Hold a fixed reply only for a leftover placeholder or a made-up code; let it auto-send otherwise, and record the deal's ask (Billing Request Sent) only when the copy really went
Never: Mark a fixed reply Needs you for its own timing line, or count a copy still waiting in Approvals as sent
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Content emails go to the content contact, money emails to the billing contact
nodes.b:
When: A brand splits contacts (one person for script and video, another for invoices and payment)
Do: Send scripts, cuts and content follow-ups To the content contact (the person the email greets); send invoices and payment chases to the billing email; keep the other on Cc
Never: Never let a billing contact replying about an invoice take over the deal's Brand Email for content emails
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Every loop-in gets our take-over reply
nodes.b:
When: A creator (or their team) loops noocapcollab into a brand thread, in any wording: loop in, looped in, cc'd, added, take it over
Do: Open the deal and send the fixed loop-in reply from noocapcollab: we'll take it forward from here, please share the brief and contract in this thread
Never: Never treat a loop-in as 'still a lead, brand hasn't agreed' because the wording was past tense or slightly different
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Reply to the correct person in their own thread
nodes.b:
When: Drafting a reply to a brand thread
Do: Double-check the deal's recipient history and send replies only to the person who wrote the last message in the correct brand thread.
Never: Send an email to the wrong contact or mix up threads when multiple conversations exist
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Draft rejected.

nodes.l: Keep chasing an interested brand until they answer
nodes.b:
When: A brand has agreed (we accepted their rate, or the creator said yes) and owes us the contract, brief or script approval
Do: Follow up every 3 days until they answer. A contract or brief follow-up 3+ days after our last email is never too early.
Never: Never stop after a set number of follow-ups, never let a stale stage (Negotiating) or an empty Last Our Reply stop the chase, and never hold a contract follow-up as too soon.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Chris's inbox is collab@chriscordero.net, and a Message-ID is never an address
nodes.b:
When: Building To or Cc for any email, from a thread where a brand mistyped one of our inboxes or where a Message-ID slipped into the address list
Do: Use our real inboxes (collab@chriscordero.net, collab@buildroom.ai, partnerships@ninjaaitools.com, collab@automateaiconsulting.com, collab@valchy.ai) and drop anything @mail.gmail.com
Never: Copy a brand's typo of our address (ollab@chriscordero.net) or a Message-ID into Thread CC
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A tool-access email never replaces an answer to the brand's question
nodes.b:
When: A brand approves the script (or reminds us it approved it) and asks something else: when the video draft or content comes, a date, a file
Do: Hold the tool-access email and send the brand's question to Harsh first; when his answer comes, put the access ask in the same reply.
Never: Draft or send 'thanks for approving, please give access on noocaptools@gmail.com' as the only reply to an email that asked us a question.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Sign as the creator the brand is now working with
nodes.b:
When: A deal's video moved to another creator (a mix-up, a swap) and the PM writes to the brand
Do: Sign and refer to the one creator the brand was last told about ("Brad's Team" once we told them Brad shoots it), and flag the deal so its Creator field can be corrected.
Never: Name one creator in the body and sign with another creator's team, which repeats the mix-up the brand already complained about.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: No tool-access ask when the brand already gave us an account
nodes.b:
When: A brand approves a script and the PM is about to ask for access to their tool on noocaptools@gmail.com
Do: Read the thread first: if the brand already shared a login or trial account (email and password), or an earlier email of ours already asked for access on noocaptools@gmail.com (any earlier campaign in the same thread, the account stays on), skip the tool-access email. Greet the contact by the name they sign with, never by a non-Latin display name.
Never: Ask for access the brand already gave, or greet someone by their email display name ("Hi 이승주") when they sign as "Seungjoo".
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Never say 'here is' something the email does not carry
nodes.b:
When: A brand asks for a file, image, caption, link or document we don't have on the deal yet
Do: Only write 'here is X' or 'attached is X' when X is attached or pasted in the email. If we don't have it, ask Harsh for it and draft the reply once it arrives.
Never: Draft 'Here is the cover image and caption' (or any 'please find attached') with nothing attached, and never label a request as the brand only acknowledging receipt.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: An email that just went out is never drafted a second time
nodes.b:
When: The PM is about to write a script, follow-up or other email on a deal where one of the same kind was sent in the last few hours
Do: Check PM OUTBOX for a Sent row of the same kind on the deal before drafting. A sent row means the job is done, even if the deal fields have not caught up yet.
Never: Write a second copy of the same email minutes after the first auto-sent because the deal's Script Sent Date or Last Our Reply was not updated yet.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A nudge is dead once the brand answers it, even minutes before it sends
nodes.b:
When: A follow-up, tool-access nudge or check-in has finished its 30-minute hold and is about to send
Do: Look at the thread itself for a brand email newer than the draft right before sending; if there is one, retire the nudge and read their email
Never: Never send 'any news on access?' after the brand has written that access is given
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Never give a brand a code, ID, status or date nobody supplied
nodes.b:
When: Writing any email that would contain a UID, account ID, promo or ad code, link, production status (filming, editing), an agreed date, or a confirmation that we tried something (logged in, accessed an account, received credits)
Do: Use only values that appear word for word in the brand's email, the deal, the video card or Harsh's WhatsApp answer. If the brand asked for one we don't have, leave it out of the email and ask Harsh on WhatsApp for it
Never: Never make up a number or code, never say we are filming when the card is not past 6- To Film, never accept a new post date Harsh has not agreed, never confirm we can access an account or tool nobody on our side has said they logged in to
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: An email held for a second read still counts as the brand writing last
nodes.b:
When: The two readers disagree on what a brand email means and the email is held for Harsh
Do: Record the brand's reply on the deal anyway (Last Brand Reply, Message ID, Follow-ups Sent back to 0) and read the held email before drafting any follow-up on that deal
Never: Never send a follow-up or check-in on a deal whose newest brand email is held or unread, and never ask a brand for feedback it already gave
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Never invent terms the thread never set
nodes.b:
When: Replying to a brand's brief or question about timing
Do: Only state timelines and conditions that the thread or Deal Memory already holds; if the brief asks for a pick or a date the team or Harsh decides, leave it to the script or ask Harsh
Never: Write conditions like 'within 3 business days of the signed agreement and deposit' when no agreement or deposit was ever discussed, or re-ask our own last question back to the brand
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Never say we sent something we only asked for
nodes.b:
When: Writing a follow-up or reply that refers to an earlier step (a contract, brief, script, invoice)
Do: Check the deal history for who sent it. If the brand still owes it, name it as theirs: 'any news on the contract and brief from the OiiOii team?'
Never: Never write 'the brief and contract we sent' when our email only asked for them, and never record our ask as 'us: sent contract' in Deal Memory.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: An email we send only answers what it was about
nodes.b:
When: The PM sends an automatic email (tool access, follow-up, script) in a thread where another draft is waiting with a brand question for Harsh
Do: Keep the waiting question alive: the auto email only closes drafts of its own kind, and a brand question about a date, money or files still goes to Harsh on WhatsApp.
Never: Let an automatic email silently reject a 'Needs you' reply that carried the brand's question.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A follow-up waits from our newest email, even one sent minutes ago
nodes.b:
When: Deciding whether a brand has gone quiet long enough for a follow-up, especially in the same run that just sent a cut or script
Do: Count the wait from the latest email we sent in the thread (the cut or script just sent included) and only chase 3 days after it
Never: Never draft a 'have you had a chance to review' follow-up right after we delivered something, counted from an older Last Our Reply
Seen 4 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: No follow-up to the brand while we owe the next cut or script
nodes.b:
When: A cut or script went to the brand, they sent changes (or asked for a reshoot or a revised script), and our team is working on it, even if the card or deal stage still says we are waiting on them.
Do: Treat the EDIT TRACKER row on Changes (or a Next Action like "editor making the brand's changes" or a reshoot) as our move. Send the revised cut when it is done; if it is late, tell Harsh once.
Never: Never send the brand a check-in that only repeats our last email or promises the cut 'in the next few days'.
Seen 3 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A follow-up counts from the brand's newest message, in any inbox
nodes.b:
When: A brand writes on a deal from or to the creator's own inbox (not the noocapcollab thread), e.g. 'sent it to the client for review'
Do: Record that message on the deal (Last Brand Reply, memory) and wait 3 days from it before a gentle nudge that acknowledges what they said.
Never: Send 'do you have any feedback yet?' hours after the brand told us the script is with their client.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Count every follow-up in the thread, not just the counter
nodes.b:
When: Deciding whether to send another follow-up on a script or video the brand hasn't answered
Do: Count the follow-ups in the deal's history since the brand last wrote (including ones sent by hand). At 5 for a script, stop and hand it to Harsh once.
Never: Draft a follow-up numbered from a stale counter, or promise to start work 'right away' to push a silent brand.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A waiting draft dies once the brand has moved past it
nodes.b:
When: A draft is waiting in Approvals and the brand writes again on that deal (in any of our inboxes, including the creator's own)
Do: Before a waiting draft goes out, read the brand's newest message on the deal and the matching Lead. If it answers or overtakes the draft (they got the file, they forwarded it to the client, they asked something new), reject the draft and answer the newest email instead.
Never: Leave a 'did you get it?' or 'just making sure this reached you' draft waiting after the brand has already confirmed receipt or acted on it.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Answer the brand's newest email, to the person who wrote it
nodes.b:
When: Replying in a thread where the brand's latest email changes the subject (hands payment to a colleague, pitches a new brand, asks a rate)
Do: Read the newest message first. Greet and address whoever wrote it, answer exactly what it asks, and send a rate or new-brand question to Harsh (it opens its own Inbound deal).
Never: Answer an older question nobody asked again, greet someone who did not write, or skip the question the brand actually asked.
Seen 8 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Copy the deal's full Thread CC on every draft
nodes.b:
When: Writing any email to a brand, including a resend from a creator's inbox
Do: Put every address in the deal's Thread CC into Cc, plus noocapcollab when the brand was asked to reply all.
Never: Send with only part of the Thread CC, or drop the creator's own team address.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

When: Writing any email
Do: Sign as the deal's own creator ('Best, Lindsay's Team'). Greet by first name only when the brand signed with it, else 'Hi there,'.
Never: Sign as another creator, leave <UNKNOWN>, or take a name from an email address or brand name.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

nodes.l: Go-live dates come from the video card
nodes.b:
When: Mentioning when a video posts
Do: Use the video card's POST DATE, and only when it is given in the facts.
Never: Use the deal's Deadline or a date from an old email.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

When: Writing any email
Do: Use commas, full stops or 'and'.
Never: Use em or en dashes.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

When: Drafts wait in Approvals
Do: Let unsent first replies to brand pitches expire after 5 days; reject drafts that the thread already moved past.
Never: Leave stale drafts piling up.
Seen 3 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

nodes.l: Reply in the brand's existing thread
nodes.b:
When: Sending any email to a brand
Do: Reply in the thread the deal already has (Thread ID / Message ID).
Never: Start a new thread when one exists.
Seen 3 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

nodes.l: Chase every cut that is with the brand
nodes.b:
When: A cut was sent for approval and the brand is silent
Do: Follow up on the normal rhythm, even if an earlier reel of the deal is posted.
Never: Treat the deal as done because reel 1 is posted.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

nodes.l: Address the brand contact of this deal
nodes.b:
When: Writing or editing a brand email
Do: Send to whoever at THIS brand wrote last in THIS thread.
Never: Use another brand's address, or apply a message about one brand to another brand's draft.
Seen 3 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

When: Writing any email
Do: Give the thing if we have it, otherwise leave the promise out.
Never: Write 'shortly', 'within a few hours', 'we'll send it today', [DATE], [name] or invented dates.
Seen 20 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

# PM lessons: Other

Mistakes the PM made once and the rule that came out of each.

nodes.l: An hourly heartbeat job must sit on a tick that has time left
nodes.b:
When: Adding or moving a once-an-hour or once-a-day job in lib/heartbeat.js
Do: Gate jobs that run after the Invoices step with hourlyTailTick(tickMin), where tickMin is the minute the tick STARTED (read once from T0), and check PM RUNS steps show the job actually running
Never: Gate a job at the end of the tick on minute < 10 (the :04 tick, always out of time), and never read new Date().getUTCMinutes() when the step is reached: the :14 tick reaches its tail at minute 16
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Tests must not read live Vercel env vars
nodes.b:
When: Adding code that reads a Vercel env var (AI_PAUSED_UNTIL, PM_AI_PROVIDER, GEMINI_API_KEY and the like) on a path the tests exercise
Do: Clear or pin that env var in both the npm test and vercel-build scripts, and run the tests once with the live value set before pushing
Never: Never let a test pass locally but depend on an env var that is set differently on Vercel, because a failed build leaves production on the old commit silently
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: One alert, one post, however many PM copies are running
nodes.b:
When: Any alert to #pm-alerts or WhatsApp, including the Claude-down notice
Do: Write a claim row first, wait a few seconds, re-read the claims and post only if ours is the earliest (ties go to the smallest page id)
Never: Never post an alert just because the log showed nothing a moment ago, since several Vercel copies check at the same second and all post
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A system alert goes out once, not once per copy of the PM
nodes.b:
When: The PM wants to tell Harsh about a lasting condition (Claude out, Gemini in use, a key failing)
Do: Check the AGENT LOG for the same alert in the last hours before posting, and log it when posting, so every Vercel instance shares the one record
Never: Never rely on an in-memory 'already sent' flag: each Vercel instance starts fresh, so the alert repeats on every cold start
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: An AI outage error keeps its root cause at the front, so cut error text still raises the r
nodes.b:
When: Both Claude and the Gemini fallback fail and the error text is cut before it is logged or checked for alerts
Do: Put the first provider's reason (Claude's spend limit, no credit) at the start of the combined error, so every slice still shows it and the spend-limit alert to Harsh fires once
Never: Never append the root cause after a long provider body; api/inbox.js and api/leads.js cut errors to 300 characters and the alert then never fires
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: When every AI provider fails, the error must say why each one failed
nodes.b:
When: An AI call falls back from Claude to Gemini and Gemini fails too
Do: Keep Claude's own error next to Gemini's in the thrown message, so PM RUNS shows the real cause and the spend-limit alert can fire
Never: Throw only the last provider's error and hide why Claude was out
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A test bank run must finish inside Vercel's 300 s limit
nodes.b:
When: Running the test bank (/api/daily) after a commit, a new lesson or at night
Do: Stop starting cases at 170 s and give up on any single case after 55 s, counting it as not run, so the last batch and the write-back always fit.
Never: Start cases right up to the limit with no cap per case, so a slow model call gets the whole run killed and its results lost.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Never repeat an action that posts or sends
nodes.b:
When: Testing or triggering a hook that posts to Discord, WhatsApp or email
Do: Wait until the new deployment is READY, dry-run first, then call it once.
Never: Never call a sending hook in a retry or polling loop.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Claude.

nodes.l: When the AI can't run, Harsh hears it once, straight away
nodes.b:
When: Claude calls fail with a spend limit or no credit ("You have reached your specified API usage limits", "credit balance")
Do: Send one ⚠️ alert that brand emails are not being read and that the spend limit needs raising at console.anthropic.com, then keep the emails unread so they are processed once it is raised
Never: Never keep retrying emails for hours without telling anyone; never mark them as handled
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.

# PM lessons: Payments

Mistakes the PM made once and the rule that came out of each.

When: Stripe already showed a brand's payment and marked the deal Paid, then the brand emails that finance has paid
Do: Record the email on the deal (Last Brand Reply) and stop there: Harsh already heard about the money from Stripe.
Never: Never send a second 'Paid' WhatsApp for the same payment, and never ask Harsh to check money Stripe already showed as arrived.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: When Stripe shows the brand's payment arrived, thank them without asking Harsh
nodes.b:
When: A brand says it paid, or the PM was waiting on proof, and the creator's Stripe shows the invoice paid (or a real receipt came)
Do: Send the fixed payment_received_thanks reply in the brand's thread on its own, once, and drop any 'send us the proof' draft
Never: Never ask Harsh whether to thank a brand whose Stripe invoice is paid, and never count the brand's own 'we paid' (even rewritten into the deal memory) as proof
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Money paid in Stripe is marked Paid everywhere  deal and Revenue sheet
nodes.b:
When: The Stripe check finds an invoice paid
Do: Mark the deal Paid and tick the matching Revenue row Paid with the payment date, so the dashboard moves it out of Awaiting payment
Never: Never leave a Revenue row under Awaiting payment once Stripe shows the invoice paid
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Creator's billing address and Tax ID stay off invoices
nodes.b:
When: Raising or emailing an invoice for a creator whose Creator Payment Details has a Billing Address or Tax ID
Do: Use those only for contracts; the invoice carries the brand's details, the amount and the pay link (bank details only when the brand asks)
Never: Never print or write the creator's own billing address or Tax ID on an invoice, its PDF or the invoice email
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Billing ask on video approval sends on its own
nodes.b:
When: The brand approves the final video or tells us to publish it, and we have no company details yet
Do: Send the fixed reply billing_on_approval straight away: we'll post as soon as possible and share the live link, please send your company billing details so the invoice goes with it
Never: Never hold this ask for Harsh's approval, and never wait until after posting to ask for billing details
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Billing details in a brand email are always saved
nodes.b:
When: A brand replies with its company name, address and tax ID for the invoice
Do: Save them to Billing Details on the deal and raise the invoice; if the first invoice was sent by hand, tell Harsh the rest of the fee is waiting
Never: Never leave billing details only in the deal memory, and never skip a posted deal's remaining invoice in silence
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Billing asks must not run out of time
nodes.b:
When: A deal is Approved or Posted and the brand's company details aren't on file
Do: Ask for the billing details in the same heartbeat, ahead of the slow payment checks on invoices already sent
Never: Never leave a deal that needs a billing ask at the end of the Invoices list where the step runs out of time
Seen 2 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Ask for company details when the brand approves the video
nodes.b:
When: The brand approves the final video and says to publish
Do: Ask for their billing details right away, so the invoice goes out together with the live link.
Never: Never wait until after posting to ask for billing details.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Greet the person the email is going to
nodes.b:
When: Writing any email, above all a payment chase that goes to a finance or payments address rather than the usual contact
Do: Greet whoever is in To by the name they signed with (the payments team's Pavinder, not the campaign contact), and keep the usual contact on Cc
Never: Never open with the campaign contact's name while the email goes to a different person or team address
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A due date in a brand email comes from the brand's terms
nodes.b:
When: Writing a payment chase or reminder that names a due date
Do: Quote a due date only when the thread or the deal's Payment Terms give it (Net 30 agreed, the brand's own 'paid on 13/11'). When no terms were agreed, ask when we can expect the payment instead. Match the count: two invoices sent = 'the two invoices'.
Never: Quote a due date that was filled in as a Net 30 guess, or call two invoices 'the invoice'.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: One invoice email per Stripe invoice
nodes.b:
When: Drafting an invoice email for a Stripe invoice, from WhatsApp or from the heartbeat
Do: Before drafting, look for an Approvals row with the same Stripe invoice id that is waiting or already sent; if there is one, draft nothing. With split terms (part upfront, part after publication) the final invoice waits until the video is live, whatever the stage or an earlier invoice request says.
Never: Draft a second invoice or payment-chase email for an invoice that already has one, or put two cards for one invoice in front of Harsh.
Seen 4 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Chase payment where the brand said invoices go
nodes.b:
When: A brand names a finance or accounts address for invoices, or asks for reminders in the invoice thread
Do: Send invoices and every payment chase to that address, in the thread where the invoice went, with the usual contact on Cc.
Never: Never chase payment in the contact's deal thread once the brand named a finance address, and never put an estimated date in a brand email.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Answer the brand's question before chasing money
nodes.b:
When: A payment chase is due but the brand's latest email to us is a question we have not answered
Do: Hold the chase. Get the answer (ask Harsh on WhatsApp if only he knows) and send that first; the payment ask can ride in the same email.
Never: Draft a payment chase that skips or guesses the answer to the brand's open question.
Seen 3 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Chase where the brand told us to chase
nodes.b:
When: Writing a payment chase or reminder on a deal where the brand said how invoices or reminders must be sent (which thread, which finance address, which portal)
Do: Read the thread for the brand's own instructions first and follow them: reply in the thread the invoice went out in and copy the finance address they named. If the deal's Thread ID points at the old collab thread, switch it to the invoice thread before drafting.
Never: Chase in the collab thread without finance when the brand asked for the invoice thread with finance in copy, or send a second chase the same day as one already sent by hand.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Invoiced only when an invoice really went out
nodes.b:
When: Reading an email that mentions an invoice, or creating a deal from an old thread
Do: Move a deal to Invoiced only when our invoice was actually sent (Approvals, Stripe, or the creator's own invoice to the brand) and record its date. When the brand sends billing details, raise the invoice; asking for details is not invoicing.
Never: Never set Invoiced or Paid from the AI's reading of an email, and never leave a deal at Invoiced with no invoice date, number or Stripe invoice.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Stop chasing billing details after 3 reminders or when the brand pays through a platform
nodes.b:
When: The video is posted and the invoice needs the brand's company details
Do: Count Billing Reminders Sent. At 3, stop and tell Harsh once. If the brand pays through Gusto, Faved, creator.co or a similar portal, use that portal and don't ask for invoice details. Never nudge while our own latest email in the thread is still unanswered.
Never: Draft a 4th billing reminder, or a reminder hours after our last email.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

When: A brand says 'we've already paid' with nothing attached
Do: Check Stripe, then earlier proof in the deal that is dated on or after THIS invoice; if neither, ask for the transfer receipt or reference.
Never: Mark it paid, use proof of an earlier payment (a first half, an old invoice) for a later invoice, or ask again for proof they already sent for this invoice.
Seen 6 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

nodes.l: Upfront money does not close the deal
nodes.b:
When: A payment arrives before the video is posted
Do: Record it as an upfront part payment and keep the deal open.
Never: Mark the whole deal Paid.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

nodes.l: Brand asked for the invoice = raise it
nodes.b:
When: A brand asks for the invoice
Do: Draft the invoice right away, To the address the brand named for invoices (Brad is invoiced by hand, never flag his Stripe). If the fee is missing on the deal, ask Harsh once for it instead of writing a reply.
Never: Reply that it will come later.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

nodes.l: Retire a before-due reminder after the due date
nodes.b:
When: A payment chase is waiting and the due date passes
Do: Replace it with a real past-due chase.
Never: Send 'is it on track for the due date' after the date.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

When: A brand writes about paying
Do: Only Stripe showing it paid, or a receipt / transfer reference, counts as paid. 'In our payment queue', 'scheduled', 'will be paid on' = note the date and keep it Invoiced.
Never: Mark Paid from a promise, ask for proof of a payment that hasn't happened, or send an 'is it on track' check-in before the date the brand already gave.
Seen 4 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

nodes.l: Invoice emails are one line plus payment details
nodes.b:
When: Writing an invoice email
Do: One sentence and the payment details.
Never: Add extra paragraphs or filler.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

# PM lessons: Video & editors

Mistakes the PM made once and the rule that came out of each.

nodes.l: Hashtags are the post caption, not changes to the cut
nodes.b:
When: A brand whose reel is approved or cleared to post asks only for different hashtags or caption tags
Do: Keep the video where it is (To Post), put the hashtags on the card's Post Caption, tell whoever posts, and get the reel live with them, then send the live link.
Never: Move the tracker row or card back to Changes or send hashtag notes to the editor as video feedback.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A deleted video card never stops a brand email from being handled
nodes.b:
When: A brand email arrives for a deal whose linked card was deleted
Do: Skip the note on the deleted card and handle the rest of the email
Never: Let a Notion 'block is archived' error fail the whole email
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A brand's publish deadline means the video is ready for their review 4 days before it
nodes.b:
When: A brand gives a publish, go-live or posting deadline, asks about the timeline, or worries the deadline is tight
Do: Work back from the deadline: the video must be ready for the brand's review 3 to 4 days before the publish date (4 by default), so there is time for their review, a round of changes and posting. When several videos can't go live on the same day, plan them on separate days that all land by the deadline. Replies about timing say when the scripts and the videos will be with them, worked out this way
Never: Never plan the video to be ready on the publish deadline itself, and never answer a deadline worry with only 'that can be done' and no dates
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Drive links appear within 10 minutes of To Film
nodes.b:
When: A card moves to 6- To Film
Do: Make the Raw Footage, Assets and Edited Vid links on the next heartbeat.
Never: Never leave a To Film card without links for more than one heartbeat.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Images sent with change notes go to the editor too
nodes.b:
When: Harsh forwards change notes on WhatsApp with an image (a logo, a screenshot of the shot to fix)
Do: Send the image to the editor with the notes: into their Discord thread, under the notes on the intake row and on the video card.
Never: Never pass on only the words when the message carried an image the editor needs.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: One brand email can carry two asks, and both get acted on
nodes.b:
When: A brand email does more than one thing, like approving video 1 while sending notes on scripts 2 and 3
Do: Act on every ask in it: the approved video's tracker row goes to To Post and the script notes go to the script cards. Anything not acted on goes to Harsh in #pm and the email stays unread
Never: File the whole email under one event and drop the other ask
Seen 2 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: One ping per card, and check what fires before changing anything by hand
nodes.b:
When: Claude or the team makes a card, moves a row or queues a message by hand
Do: First work out which PM or n8n step reacts to that change (new sponsor card = Rudraksh is pinged on the next run) and let that one step do the announcing
Never: Queue a second ping for something an automation will already announce
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Claude.

nodes.l: A script-writer flag belongs to the card it was picked on
nodes.b:
When: Send to Script Writer (Script changes, Brief changed, Concept changed) is picked on one card of a deal with several videos
Do: Move, note and link only that card. Leave the other videos' cards, and the deal's Next Action, as they are unless the flagged card is the deal's own linked video.
Never: Never move a card whose cut is with the brand back to 4- Script Draft, and never write another video's brief onto it.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A cut is 'revised' only if the brand already saw a cut
nodes.b:
When: Writing the email that hands a cut to the brand after our own team or Harsh asked for changes before the brand saw anything
Do: Call it the cut for their review. Say it is the revised cut with their changes only when the brand saw an earlier cut and asked for those changes
Never: Never tell a brand 'here is the revised cut with the changes you asked for' when they never saw a cut or asked for changes
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A brand approving the cut moves the tracker row to To Post, even when the second reader on
nodes.b:
When: A brand writes that the draft or cut is approved ("looks great, approved!", "go ahead and publish"), even while asking for the remaining assets or a final check
Do: Read it as video_feedback with video_approved: move the EDIT TRACKER row to To Post with Approved At, and stop chasing the brand for feedback on that cut
Never: Never hold a video approval just because the second reader calls it a plain brand_reply, and never leave the row on With Brand after the brand approved it
Seen 3 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Notes on an edited cut go to the editor, never the script writer
nodes.b:
When: Harsh forwards or types fixes with timestamps, shots, avatar, music or captions, often with a second line naming the deal ("Brad x promo cut changes")
Do: Read messages sent together as one; send cut notes to the named deal's EDIT TRACKER row as Changes so the editor is pinged
Never: Send cut notes to Rudraksh as script changes, guess the deal from the last card in the chat, or treat a deal label as the answer a brand is waiting for
Seen 2 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A cut link after script approval is a Draft video email
nodes.b:
When: Someone on WhatsApp or chat hands over an edited video link (Drive, Frame.io) to send to a brand whose script is already approved
Do: File it as Kind 'Draft video' so the deal moves to Submitted and the board card moves to 9- Approval Brand/Creator, and write one sentence that hands over the cut
Never: File a cut as a Script email or ask for 'feedback on the script' once the script is approved
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A revised cut email only hands over the cut
nodes.b:
When: Sending a cut to a brand, above all a revised cut after their changes
Do: Say in one sentence that the link is the revised cut with the changes they asked for, and nothing else. A billing or other question the brand asked in the same email goes to Harsh (WhatsApp) or its own reply.
Never: Answer the brand's earlier email inside the cut email, promise the revised cut 'for a final check' when this IS the revised cut, or ask a brand that pays through a platform (Gusto) or already got 3 billing reminders for their billing details. When the brand asks US to send billing details, never reply by asking for theirs.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Approved with one change means changes for the editor
nodes.b:
When: A brand approves a cut but asks for one change in the same email (music, a caption, a frame)
Do: Put the video's EDIT TRACKER row on Changes with the brand's words in Brand Feedback and the board card on 8- Changes, so the editor fixes it and the revised cut goes straight back to the brand. Anything else in the email (billing details, a date) is handled on its own.
Never: Hold the whole email for Harsh because the readers disagree on approval vs feedback, or treat it as a full approval and post the cut unchanged.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: One EDIT TRACKER row per video
nodes.b:
When: Adding or creating an EDIT TRACKER row for a video (by hand, from a brief page, or when an edit was delivered without the buttons)
Do: Look up existing rows with the same Video ID first. If one exists, update that row (status, dates, note) instead of adding a new one.
Never: Add a second row for a Video ID that already has one; the watcher, follow-ups and reports then count the same cut twice.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Let the n8n watcher send the editor's changes alert
nodes.b:
When: The PM sets an EDIT TRACKER row to Changes from a brand email
Do: Set Status to Changes and fill Brand Feedback only. Leave Changes Requested At empty: the n8n EDIT TRACKER watcher sends the tagged 'CHANGES REQUESTED' alert within 2 minutes and stamps that field itself. The PM's own thread post is only a fallback after 20 minutes.
Never: Never stamp Changes Requested At from the PM (it makes the watcher think the alert already went out), and never ask Harsh to add settings to fix something that used to work: find what changed.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Brand changes move the board card to 8
nodes.b:
When: A brand sends change notes on a cut that is with them
Do: Set the EDIT TRACKER row to Changes, ping the editor, and move the creator's board card back to 8- Changes at the same moment.
Never: Never leave the board card on 9- Approval while the editor is working on brand changes.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: An approved video goes live inside the brand's window
nodes.b:
When: A brand approves a cut and names publishing days
Do: The same day, put the card at 10- To Post with a POST DATE inside the brand's window and tell the team. If the date passes with nothing live, tell Harsh once with the brand's latest message. Take the invoice due date from the contract terms (Net 30 = invoice date + 30), not the Stripe default.
Never: Let an approved video sit unposted for days while the brand chases, or record it only as 'Waiting on us' with no card or date.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Cut with the brand means board card at 9
nodes.b:
When: An edited cut goes to the brand, by Send to Brand or by approving a Draft video email
Do: Move the creator's board card to 9- Approval Brand/Creator together with the EDIT TRACKER row going to With Brand, and only move it forward from 6, 7 or 8.
Never: Never leave the board card on 7- In Edit while the video is waiting on the brand.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Editor page shows the approved script
nodes.b:
When: An editor opens a video's brief page
Do: Show the approved version from the Script sub-page (the version marked approved/final, else the latest).
Never: Show no script or an old version.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

nodes.l: Editors get the brand's full notes
nodes.b:
When: Passing brand notes to an editor
Do: Send every line, and the Discord Changes alert must show them under 'What to fix'.
Never: Send only the first line, or an alert without the notes.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

nodes.l: Every Raw Footage folder is shared by link
nodes.b:
When: A Drive folder is made for a video
Do: Share it with anyone with the link before giving it out.
Never: Hand out a private folder.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

nodes.l: A cut can't wait unseen in review
nodes.b:
When: A cut is In Review on EDIT TRACKER
Do: Remind once a day, and right away when the go-live date is close.
Never: Let it sit until the post date passes.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

nodes.l: Each video's cut email stands alone
nodes.b:
When: Sending or drafting a cut for one video
Do: Only replace an older cut email for the same video (same Frame.io link or title).
Never: Reject another video's revised cut.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

nodes.l: Editor page reads each board's own column names
nodes.b:
When: Showing card fields on the editor brief page
Do: Match REF, Ref Video, Edited Vid and similar.
Never: Assume one column name for every board.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

nodes.l: Brand change notes go to the editor
nodes.b:
When: A brand sends notes on a cut or a script
Do: Put the notes on the right video row and send them to the editor (cut) or Rudraksh (script). After the editor is done, draft the revised-cut email.
Never: Reply to the brand just to acknowledge the notes.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

# PM lessons: WhatsApp

Mistakes the PM made once and the rule that came out of each.

nodes.l: A signed contract goes straight to the brand, never to Approvals
nodes.b:
When: Harsh drops a signed contract in WhatsApp, or names the brand for one the PM asked about
Do: Check signed contracts first (dropped file, or a brand name for a waiting contract) and send them in the brand's thread with no approval step
Never: Never let an older open question about the same brand claim the message, and never say an email is waiting in Approvals unless a draft was actually created
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A signed contract that identifies itself needs no brand name
nodes.b:
When: Harsh drops a signed contract PDF in the NOOCAP MEDIA chat with a caption like 'here you go'
Do: Send it when the PDF names the deal's creator by legal name, names the brand (or its agency's domain), and that brand's contract is waiting in CONTRACTS; otherwise ask which brand
Never: Never hold a signed contract just because the brand isn't in the caption when the PDF already proves which deal it is
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Only noocapcollab contracts are shared (for now)
nodes.b:
When: A brand sends a contract to a creator's own inbox (Chris, Lindsay), not to noocapcollab
Do: Share only contracts that reach noocapcollab. A creator-inbox contract is left to the creator and management (CREATOR_INBOX_CONTRACTS = false in lib/leads.js)
Never: Never save, announce on Discord or send to WhatsApp a contract that only reached a creator's own inbox
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

When: A contract arrives, possibly in more than one email (agency email plus signing-service email, or a resend)
Do: Claim the contract by its sign link (or its files and thread) before sending; if it was already sent, only file it
Never: Never send the same contract to the WhatsApp group twice, because Harsh forwards these to the creator and a second copy reaches the client again
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A WhatsApp question or contract waiting for a closed chat is saved even when the nudge fai
nodes.b:
When: A brand asks for something only Harsh or Pratham has, or a contract arrives, while their WhatsApp chat has been quiet for 24 hours
Do: Queue the question or contract in the chat first, then try the nudge template, and report a failed nudge without dropping what was queued
Never: Let a failed pm_needs_you nudge throw away the queued question, so the person never hears the brand asked
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Every revised cut on a WhatsApp deal reaches Harsh with its Frame.io link
nodes.b:
When: An editor finishes a cut (first or revised) for a WhatsApp deal, or Harsh asks for 'the link' / 'the updated link'
Do: Send Harsh the Frame.io link on WhatsApp for every round, named by round; when asked for the link, answer with the Frame.io link from EDIT TRACKER
Never: Never let an alert filter swallow a new round because its headline matches the last one, and never answer 'the link' with the Drive folder
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: WhatsApp deals get the cut link on WhatsApp
nodes.b:
When: A cut is marked Send to Brand and the deal runs on WhatsApp (or has no email deal)
Do: Send Harsh the Frame.io link and caption on WhatsApp to forward, mark the row With Brand and move the card to 9- Approval.
Never: Never bounce a WhatsApp deal's cut back to In Review with an error.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A WhatsApp message only answers the question it replies to
nodes.b:
When: The PM asked Harsh for something a brand needs (an account email, a code) and Harsh then sends an unrelated message or link
Do: Use a message as the answer only when it swipe-replies to the question or plainly gives what was asked for; otherwise ask again.
Never: Never put an unrelated link or text into a brand email as the answer, and never turn a bare "Okay", "noted" or a greeting like "Hi" into a reply that promises or agrees to anything.
Seen 4 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: Reject wins over Send, and never say nothing was sent when it was
nodes.b:
When: Send and Reject are tapped on the same draft within seconds
Do: Check the draft just before it leaves and stop if it was rejected; if it already went, say so plainly and offer a correction.
Never: Never tell Harsh 'Nothing was sent' about an email that went out.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Harsh correction.

nodes.l: A WhatsApp ask names only what Harsh alone can give
nodes.b:
When: A brand email needs work done (recording, editing, posting, a revised cut) rather than a fact, file, date or money decision from Harsh
Do: Send the work to the team or the creator through the video card and editor flow, and ask Harsh only for the missing fact (a date, a code, a price, a file only he holds). If the brand asked nothing he must answer, send him nothing.
Never: Send Harsh a swipe-reply ask whose 'need' is the team's own work (record screen recordings, send the revised draft, publish the video).
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A queued WhatsApp message is sent once
nodes.b:
When: Asks and contract alerts queued while the chat was closed go out at the morning round-up or when the chat reopens
Do: Send each queued message once and mark it sent so no later run sends it again; before sending, check the same text has not already gone out since it was queued.
Never: Send the same ask or contract alert again on every heartbeat.
Seen 2 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A file sent in the WhatsApp chat goes only to the brand named with it
nodes.b:
When: Harsh or Pratham drops a contract or file into the WhatsApp chat, with or without a caption, and sometimes names the brand in the next message
Do: Match the file to a deal only from the brand named in the caption or the very next message, the file name, or the brand's name as whole words in the contract text. If the file name names a different company than the deal (Automate AI Consulting x Auremere is Lindsay's), or the brand is unclear, ask which brand and wait.
Never: Auto-send a signed contract to a deal matched by a few letters inside the contract text, or to a deal of a different creator than the one whose company is on the file.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

When: A draft is shown to Harsh or Pratham on WhatsApp
Do: Send the draft card once; if the person writes again about the same draft, answer in text or act on it
Never: Send the same draft card twice in a row
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Add N videos  means new cards, not script notes
nodes.b:
When: Harsh tells the PM on WhatsApp to add videos, cards or a multi-video campaign for a creator
Do: Create one card per video on that creator's board (with the brief link and date he gave) under the right deal, and ask once which deal it belongs to if unclear
Never: Never turn it into 'script feedback' for Rudraksh on an existing deal
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A message about another creator or another brand never answers this question
nodes.b:
When: Harsh writes on WhatsApp while a brand question for the same brand but a different creator is open (two ElevenLabs deals, one Duncan and one Chris).
Do: Match the answer on brand AND creator. If the message names another creator or carries a 'Creator X OtherBrand' label, treat it as news for that deal (or a new deal) and leave the open question waiting.
Never: Never write a reply from a message that names a different creator, and never state facts in a brand email ("we've checked, the post is live") that nobody gave you.
Seen 3 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: A file Harsh sends is never dropped
nodes.b:
When: Harsh sends a file, code or link on WhatsApp while another draft for that brand is waiting
Do: Work out which brand and thread the file is for (ask once if unclear), then draft the email carrying that file word for word in that brand's thread, alongside any draft already waiting.
Never: Answer a file from Harsh with 'a reply for that thread is already waiting' and show the old draft instead.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Only use WhatsApp templates Meta has approved
nodes.b:
When: The 24-hour WhatsApp window is closed and the PM needs to reach Harsh or Pratham
Do: Use a template name that exists and is approved in Meta; if a send fails with 'Template name does not exist', fall back to an approved template and raise it in #pm-alerts once.
Never: Ship a new template name in code before Meta approves it, or let failed pushes fail silently.
Seen 19 time(s). Source: System check.

nodes.l: Brand requests at night are kept
nodes.b:
When: A brand asks for something while WhatsApp is quiet or closed
Do: Queue the question and deliver it with the next message or the morning round-up.
Never: Drop it.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

When: Harsh says yes to a list of changes on WhatsApp
Do: Apply all of them.
Never: Apply only the first one.
Seen 1 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

nodes.l: Ask Harsh for things only we have
nodes.b:
When: A brand asks for ad codes, a UID, an account email, a contract, files, alone or together with a script
Do: Ask Harsh on WhatsApp, then draft from his answer word for word.
Never: Draft a promise email instead.
Seen 8 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

When: Alerting Harsh
Do: Send each thing once. Discord pm alerts are mirrored to WhatsApp, so never send both.
Never: Send near-duplicate messages or ask about team work (scripts, cuts, uploads).
Seen 5 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

When: A deal came in on WhatsApp
Do: Alert Harsh (script ready, posted).
Never: Email the brand. And never send a 'Script ready, send the brand on WhatsApp' PDF for a card of an EMAIL deal (cards (2), (3) of a deal are emailed with the deal's Script email).
Seen 2 time(s). Source: Rulebook.

In one line: The Ops Manager tags an editor on a video in the client's Notion dashboard and sets its status to In Edit, the editor gets a Discord message with the video and its posting date, edits it, and then submits the Frame.io link from the script page using the Done editing button.

### What this system does
This is how a video goes from "we need this edited" to "the editor is working on it." Every client has their own dashboard in Notion where their videos and scripts live, and the Ops Manager assigns work from there. When an editor is tagged on a video in a client's dashboard and its status is changed to In Edit, they get a notification in their channel telling them which video to edit and when it's going to be posted, so they know which videos to prioritise. Editors don't need Notion access, because the script is shown to them on a simple web page, and that same page is where they hand the video back once it's done.

### How the script page works
All scripts are written and stored in Notion, inside each client's dashboard. Editors never open Notion though, because we have our own web page hosted on Vercel that reads the scripts from Notion and shows them in a clean, simple view. Think of Notion as the kitchen where scripts are made and the Vercel page as the window where editors pick them up.
- When a script is added or changed in Notion, the Vercel page shows the latest version automatically, so editors always see the newest one after a refresh.
- Editors only need the page link, with no Notion login or invite.
- Editors can read the script but can't change it, so if something in a script looks wrong, they tell the Ops Manager and it gets fixed in Notion.
- If a script is missing on the page, it usually means it hasn't been added to the client's dashboard in Notion yet.
- Each video on the page has a Done editing button. When the editor finishes, they click it and submit the Frame.io link and their name, and that sends the finished video into the review system (SOP 02).

### Who is involved
- Owner: The Ops Manager, who assigns the videos from the client dashboards
- Users: every NOOCAP editor

### When it runs
Every working day. The Ops Manager assigns about 4 to 6 videos a day, which is roughly 2 per client, and every assigned video should be finished the same day.

### Tools used

- Open the client's dashboard in Notion.

Getting paid for brand deals used to mean chasing details and making invoices by hand. nodes.l: LINDSAY — DESIGN FILE (Motion Graphics) - 1. What we deliver

- For every video we hand over: a preview (full video with graphics), a transparent overlay (HEVC with alpha, so the editor can place Lindsay in split or full screen), EDIT-NOTES with timecodes, and a CLONE.mp3 (only her on-screen lines, silences removed).

nodes.l: LINDSAY — DESIGN FILE (Motion Graphics) - 2. Pacing and retention
nodes.b:
- New graphic every ~1.8 s (1.7–2.4 s). Nothing holds longer than ~4 s without something moving inside it.
- Inside a graphic, something changes every 0.5–1 s (a card lands, a number ticks, a cursor clicks).
- Never more than 2 TOP (split) graphics in a row; the next one goes FULL.
- At least 40 % of graphics are FULL. Big reveals (the tool's name, the key screen, lists, the output file) are always FULL.
- Hook: open on Lindsay (TOP) for the first line, then go FULL on the payoff visual. No cuts until the first sentence ends.
- About 60–70 % of lines get a graphic. Lines with nothing concrete to show stay on Lindsay.

nodes.l: LINDSAY — DESIGN FILE (Motion Graphics) - 3. Safe zone (Instagram   TikTok UI)
nodes.b: Important graphics and text go in the white area. The red area only if really needed. Backgrounds and footage may fill the red area; titles, numbers, logos, labels and key UI may not.

Sampled from Lindsay's own videos (colour only — don't copy her old edits).
- One background per clip. A tool's own brand colour may replace gold for that tool's moment.

- Sans: Inter Display 700–800, tight tracking (−0.03em), sentence case. Headlines and labels.
- Emphasis: Playfair Display Italic, lowercase, for the one word that matters.
  - Regular weight next to the sans: "I built a system" (t04).
  - Black weight in green or coral when it's the word (t01).
  - Keywords in curly quotes: “cloud” (t03).
- Sizes (1080 px canvas): hero word 150–180 px · headline 96–120 px · label 44–56 px.
- One headline per graphic, max 3–4 words, never more than 2 lines.
- Open question: keep these free fonts, or switch to Lindsay's licensed brand fonts?

- Signature entry "rise + focus": every element rises from +40 px below while blurred (16 → 0 px), fades in and scales 0.96 → 1 over 0.45 s. Groups stagger 0.08–0.12 s.
- Exits: fast (0.2 s) fade + blur, or a hard cut. Most clips end on a 0.5 s hold.
- Tool name: decodes left to right, letters flicking through 2–3 glyphs (~0.5 s).
- Cross-out: icon greys in → full colour → red line draws corner to corner.
- Numbers always count up. Big money or counts use the flip counter.
- Cursor: real macOS cursor on a slight curve; click = small bounce + ripple.
- Camera: slow push-in on UIs, punch-in on the exact element. No zoom on Claude chat typing frames.
- Never: spins, bouncy text, wipes, glitch transitions, emoji, shaky cam.

    Hook 2:
Forget MCP as you know it, because companies like Cloudflare and Anthropic are moving to a setup where the model writes code to call tools instead of calling them one by one.
    Body:
So the problem is really two-fold, because every MCP call has to go out and return to the model before the next one starts, and once you've connected hundreds of tools the list by itself eats most of your context. Cloudflare's fix is called Code Mode, where tools get rewritten as a TypeScript API so the model can write one small script that chains the calls in a sandbox, and only the final answer comes back. It makes sense because these models have seen way more real code than tool calls. Anthropic's version is called programmatic tool calling, which is why I think the one-call-at-a-time way of using MCP is probably on its way out.
    CTA:
